Watch the ghost with the most this Halloween!

Join us at the Park Theatre for a FREE (!) Halloween screening of Tim Burton‘s iconic BEETLEJUICE, courtesy of our friends at Cambie Village.

Alec Baldwin and Geena Davis star as Adam and Barbara Maitland, a sweetly dull New England couple who die in a car crash and return as ghosts to their beloved country house. Their timing is terrible: the house has just been bought by the Deetzes, a family of insufferable New Yorkers with very strong opinions about interior design. When their own amateur hauntings fail to clear the place out, the Maitlands call on a freelance “bio-exorcist” from the other side. Word of advice: whatever you do, don’t say his name three times. With Michael Keaton, Winona Ryder, Catherine O’Hara.

Event better? After the free(!) screening, you can head on over to check out the rest of Cambie Village’s Halloween festivities and celebrations at the Plaza on West 18th. Get ready for a haunted house, trick-or-treating, live music, pumpkin decorating at the Choices Market tents, and more.

Costumes are welcome and very encouraged!

Saturday, October 31
Doors 9:30 am | Movie 10:30 am *Start time subject to change. Please arrive on time.

Please note: Guests must be scanned in by 9:45 am. If seats are not claimed by 9:45 am, seating will become available at the door upon entry.

BEETLEJUICE (Tim Burton, 1988 / PG / 92 mins) Newly dead and stuck haunting their own house, Adam and Barbara Maitland are horrified when a pretentious family moves in and starts redecorating. Unable to frighten the living on their own, the ghostly couple summon Betelgeuse, a lewd and unpredictable freelance spirit who promises results. But once he has been called, Betelgeuse turns out to be far harder to get rid of than the people they wanted gone.

In this 1980 sci-fi horror film, William Hurt plays Eddie Jessup, a scientist obsessed with discovering mankind’s true role in the universe. To this end, he submits himself to a series of mind-expanding experiments. By enclosing himself in a sensory-deprivation chamber and taking hallucinogenic drugs, Jessup hopes to explore different levels of human consciousness, but instead is devolved into an apelike monster. Director Ken Russell helmed ALTERED STATES from a script by Paddy Chayefsky, who adapted his own novel of the same name. With William Hurt, Blair Brown, Drew Barrymore, Bob Balaban.

Wednesday, October 21
Doors 9:00 pm | Movie 9:30 pm

ALTERED STATES (Ken Russell, 1980 / 18A / 102 mins) Respected Harvard scientist and psychology professor Edward Jessup decides to combine his experiments in sensory deprivation tanks with powerful hallucinogenic drugs, convinced that it may help him unlock different states of consciousness. The experiments are a success at first, but as Jessup continues his work, he begins to experience altered mental and also physical states. As he spends more time in sensory deprivation, his grip on reality begins to slip away.

Between 1943 and 1944, General de Gaulle works to unite a deeply divided French Resistance, wins legitimacy for Free France from reluctant Allies like Franklin D. Roosevelt, and orchestrates the liberation of the country. Directed by Antonin Baudry, with Simon Abkarian, Niels Schneider and Anamaria Vartolomei.

Individual tickets available as listed.

Sunday, November 8

DE GAULLE: LIBERTÉ (Antonin Baudry, 2026 / 160 mins / PG) The war turns, and de Gaulle fights a second battle at home and abroad. He has to hold a fractured Resistance together and persuade Roosevelt and the other Allies that Free France deserves a seat at the table, all while the liberation of France draws closer.

A co-presentation with Park Theatre and Visions Ouest Productions | Rendez-Vous French Film Festival (with the hyperlink), in collaboration with Alliance Française Vancouver, SFU Live & Le Relais francophone.

In June 1940, as France collapses and signs the armistice with Nazi Germany, an unknown French general named Charles de Gaulle refuses to surrender. With no army, no official mandate, and no backing, he flees to London to launch the Free France Forces and convince the world that the fight is not over. Slowly, rebellious students, determined soldiers, and figures like Jean Moulin begin to rise up and join the cause across England, France, and Africa.

DE GAULLE: RESISTANCE (Antonin Baudry, 2026 / 159 mins / PG ) France falls in June 1940, and one unknown general will not accept it. Charles de Gaulle escapes to London with no army and no backing, determined to prove that France’s war is far from over. Based on the book De Gaulle: Une certaine idée de la France by Julian Jackson.

A co-presentation with Park Theatre and Visions Ouest Productions | Rendez-Vous French Film Festival (with the hyperlink), in collaboration with Alliance Française Vancouver, SFU Live & Le Relais francophone.

Handsome, shallow, and ultra-muscular, Jim Queen is a gay influencer content to live off his looks. Thin, insecure, and closeted, Lucien is one of Jim’s many followers. When the gym-bod god gets infected with Heterosis — a drug manufactured by the far-right that causes heterosexuality — the two men must join forces and find a cure for straightness before Jim’s online clout runs out.

Brought to life by directors Marco Nguyen and Nicolas Athané, JIM QUEEN is a perfect satirical creation: Jim’s vanity and superficiality make for a great sendup of gay “body fascism”. Of course, the filmmakers reserve much of their scorn for homophobic conservatism, and the inversion of homo- and heterosexuality is provocative and hilarious. From the opening musical number to the spoof of conversion therapy to an outrageous Trojan-horse gag and beyond, JIM QUEEN is a raucous delight.

Audience Award, VIFF 2026

Be Afraid. Be Very Afraid.

In 1986, Canadian filmmaker David Cronenberg cemented his iconic status thanks to this bold remake of THE FLY, a wildly imaginative work of poignant, weirdly romantic body horror that perfectly showcases his darkest sensibilities, dry humour, and a masterful understanding of the devastating potential of practical VFX.

In what is easily a career defining performance, Jeff Goldblum stars with Geena Davis (at one time, they were the tallest real-life couple in Hollywood) as Seth Brundle, a self-involved research scientist, and Veronica Quaife, a science-magazine reporter. Inviting Veronica to his lab, Seth prepares to demonstrate his “telepod,” which can theoretically transfer matter through space. As they grow closer over the next few weeks, she inadvertently goads Seth into experimenting with human beings rather than inanimate objects. Seth himself enters the telepod, preparing to transmit himself through the ether — but he doesn’t know that he is sharing the telepod with a tiny housefly.

THE FLY (David Cronenberg, 1986 / 96 mins / PG) When Seth Brundle makes a huge scientific and technological breakthrough in teleportation, he decides to test it on himself. Unbeknownst to him, a common housefly manages to get inside the device and the two become one.

Filmmaker Matt Johnson (NIRVANNA THE BAND THE SHOW THE MOVIE, OPERATION AVALANCHE) narrative feature TONY offers a thoughtful origin story for a rebellious voice that defined a generation in a 19-year-old Anthony Bourdain (Dominic Sessa, THE HOLDOVERS) as he stumbles into the chaotic world of a Cape Cod restaurant kitchen. The setting kicks off a summer that will shape the course of his life. With Antonio Banderas, Emilia Jones.

TONY (Matt Johnson, 2026 / 106 mins / 14A) A 19-year-old Anthony Bourdain travels to Provincetown and stumbles into the chaotic world of a restaurant kitchen, setting off a summer that will shape the course of his life.

FATHERLAND centers on the relationship between the Nobel Prize-winning writer Thomas Mann (Hans Zischler) and his daughter Erika (Oscar-nominee Sandra Hüller, ANATOMY OF A FALL ) — actress, writer and rally driver. In the summer of 1949, at the height of the Cold War, father and daughter embark on a challenging and emotional road trip in a black Buick taking them across a Germany in ruins — from US dominated Frankfurt to Soviet controlled Weimar. Returning home after sixteen years in exile in the US, Thomas Mann has to face not only a divided fatherland, but also a deep fracture within his own family. With FATHERLAND, acclaimed filmmaker Pawel Pawlikowski picks up where he left off with his award-winning IDA and COLD WAR, exploring — in his elliptic, distilled style — the themes of identity, family, love and guilt amid the turmoil and confusion of post-war Europe.

Winner, Palm d’Or Best Director, Cannes Film Festival 2026

Opens at the Park Theatre on Friday, October 30
Complete showtimes, info and tickets on sale Monday, October 12.

FATHERLAND (Pawel Pawlikowski, 2026 / 82 mins / PG / Polish & German w. EST) At the height of the Cold War, ‘Fatherland’ centers on the relationship between the writer Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika—actress, writer and rally driver—as they embark on a road trip in a black Buick cruiser across a Germany in ruins.

When a basket maker constructs a wicker husband for a local fisherwoman, he proves more spectacular than she ever could have imagined. His soulful spirit and unique prowess soon awakens something inside her, setting off a wave of jealousy, fascination and upheaval that threatens the very fabric of her village. With Olivia Colman, Alexander Skarsgård, Peter Dinklage, Elizabeth Debicki, Richard E. Grant.

WICKER (Alex Huston Fischer & Eleanor Wilson, 2026 / 14A / 105 mins) An ostracized fisherwoman commissions the local basketmaker to weave her a husband, but when her wicker creation proves unexpectedly extraordinary, his presence ignites jealousy and upheaval that threatens their quiet village.

MENOPAUSE: COMING IN HOT is a powerful documentary that challenges the traditional narrative around menopause—redefining it as an empowering transition, rather than a stigmatizing one.

Filmmakers in attendance for post-screening Q&A.

Sunday, November 1
Doors 12:00 pm | Event 12:45 pm *Start time subject to change. Please arrive on time.
Tickets HERE

General public tickets on sale October 17 at 8:00 am.

When a strong-willed perimenopausal documentary filmmaker is told there isn’t a lot of help available for her symptoms, she goes on a mission to find out more about menopause, and ends up on a quest that makes her relearn everything she thought she knew about aging.

MENOPAUSE: COMING IN HOT s a thought-provoking, tongue-in-cheek documentary that follows filmmaker Kate Green into the most overlooked and misunderstood phase of a woman’s life — menopause. The film ventures where few documentaries dare to go, taking viewers on a whirlwind journey through the physical, emotional, and societal aspects of menopause, bringing to light a topic that has long been shrouded in silence, while hopefully helping Kate remember where she put her car keys.

In Canada, about 47% of our food is wasted. Want to do something about it? 

Join Food Stash Foundation for its 10 Year Anniversary Celebration screening of JUST EAT IT: A FOOD WASTE STORY. Plus, we’ll have a raffle, prizes and a chance to get involved in the fight against food waste. It’s an evening you won’t want to miss!

After catching a glimpse of the billions of dollars of good food that is tossed each year in North America, filmmakers and food lovers Jen and Grant pledge to quit grocery shopping cold turkey and survive only on foods that would otherwise be thrown away.

Come early to meet the Food Stash team and learn about our work, get your raffle tickets, and enjoy our pre-show programming.

Plus, eligible donations to Food Stash will be matched to help rescue twice as much good food, and provide twice as many meals to the community. Sign up for the Food Stash newsletter to learn more: https://www.foodstash.ca/newsletter-signup

Tuesday, November 10

Tickets HERE

Donations to Food Stash will be matched dollar-for-dollar for a limited time, thanks to South Flats by PCI Developments and Low Tide Properties, to help rescue and redistribute twice as much food to the community. (Charity #748078524RR0001. To receive a tax receipt for your donation of $10 or more, please provide your legal name, email address, and full mailing address. Receipts will be emailed to donors following the event. The cost of your film ticket is not eligible for a tax receipt, but proceeds from this event will still support Food Stash.)

“The restoration of the material is like cleaning the Sistine Chapel with saliva. I’ve never seen the movie until I saw this restoration.” Guillermo del Toro

An enduring masterpiece of cinema starring Oliver Reed and Vanessa Redgrave, KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption – and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is the uncut and unfiltered theatrical experience that Russell always envisioned – and the first time the film will be presented restored and in 4K.

Over 164,472 frames of 35mm film were restored to bring to life KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS. Assembled from the original camera negative, this new 4K restoration presents Ken Russell’s definitive vision of The Devils by referencing the edit he privately constructed in 2004. The film’s sound has been remastered from original English Composite 35mm Mag Film, transferred at 96kHz, plus other original film elements in selected spots as needed. The Picture and Sound restoration was performed by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color, and Warner Bros. Sound. 

THE DEVILS (Ken Russell, 1971 / 117 mins / 14A) In 17th-century France, Father Urbain Grandier’s protection of the city of Loudun from the corrupt Cardinal Richelieu is undermined by a sexually repressed nun’s accusation of witchcraft.

The 10th anniversary TMFF returns to Vancouver with new films and a celebration of motorcycle culture.

An evening celebrating the stories, people, and places that make motorcycle culture what it is.

For ten years, TMFF has brought riders, filmmakers, and storytellers together through motorcycle films.

This November, we’re coming to the Park Theatre for an evening of films, conversations, and the kinds of stories that remind us why motorcycles matter in the first place.

There are long-distance journeys, personal obsessions, old bikes with stories of their own, racing, craftsmanship, friendship, loss, discovery, and a few people doing things the hard way simply because that’s how they wanted to do them.

Come early. Grab a drink. Run into people you know. Meet a few you don’t. Then settle in and watch these stories where they belong—on the big screen.

Your ticket includes access to the full evening of films. To see the full line-up and description of films visit www.motorcyclefilmfest.com/vancouver
